reports.title: Índice de Preço no Consumidor (IPC)
reports.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estatística (INE), São Tomé e Príncipe
reports.description: UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF/G.23, AFRISTAT/CPLP technical-capacity link to the CPI corroborated via INE's international-cooperation page): INE-STP's own 'Cooperação Internacional' page states directly that AFRISTAT and CPLP (Comunidade dos Países de Língua Portuguesa), among other multilateral/regional partners, have contributed technical capacity specifically to statistical domains including the CPI: "...Regionais: o Banco Africano de Desenvolvimento (BAD), AFRISTAT, CPLP, que têm tido um papel primordial para o instituto... na capacitação técnica em vários domínios, tais como a legislação, planeamento, classificações, conceitos e nomenclaturas, infraestruturas estatísticas, produção estatística, onde se destaca o índice de preços no consumidor (IPC), cartografia censitária, censos da população, contas nacionais..." — a second, independent primary source (distinct from st-snds-2018-2021) naming AFRISTAT's CPI role, plus a newly-named partner (CPLP) not previously tied to CPI work in this corpus. See new st-ine-ipc -> afristat-ihpc-guide-2014 'cites' edge in st-g23-municipal.json. São Tomé and Príncipe's national CPI. INE-STP's own site describes the index only in general terms ("um indicador que tem por finalidade medir a evolução no tempo dos preços... não é... um indicador do nível de preços... mas antes um indicador da sua variação" [an indicator meant to measure price changes over time... not a price-level indicator but a variation indicator]) — base year, publication frequency, and any COICOP/IMF-Manual citation could NOT be confirmed this round despite targeted search. Press coverage confirms a 17.0% cumulative inflation figure for December 2023, with data noted as "collected in the city of São Tomé" specifically (geographic coverage limitation, self-disclosed by the press source). The IMF's 2025 Article IV/ECF Review ("Headline CPI inflation averaged 14.4 percent in 2024") uses INE-STP's CPI figures but its own report does not document INE-STP's methodology.
reports.cadence_note: Frequency not independently confirmed this round.

reports.title: Sistema Estatístico Nacional — Estratégia Nacional de Desenvolvimento da Estatística (SNDS) 2018-2021
reports.publisher: Governo de São Tomé e Príncipe / UNFPA
reports.description: São Tomé and Príncipe's 2018-2021 national statistics strategy, hosted by UNFPA. States directly: "Peritos do AFRISTAT e outros consultores puderam melhorar o nível do pessoal responsável pelas contas nacionais e IHPC" [AFRISTAT experts and other consultants were able to improve the skill level of staff responsible for national accounts and the harmonised CPI (IHPC)] — a direct link between AFRISTAT and the country's CPI work specifically, unusually strong for a country this small. Also states the African Charter on Statistics has been "em vigor desde 2015" [in force since 2015] for São Tomé and Príncipe — this ratification year conflicts with the newer st-ende-2025-2029 document's "2016" date; recorded as an unresolved discrepancy.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational strategy document (2018-2021 planning horizon, since superseded by st-ende-2025-2029).

reports.title: Estratégia Nacional de Desenvolvimento da Estatística (ENDE) de STP 2025-2029
reports.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estatística (INE), São Tomé e Príncipe
reports.description: The current (2025-2029) national statistics strategy, INE-STP's own document. States: "o seu compromisso com a consolidação de um sistema estatístico robusto, moderno e alinhado com... a Carta Africana de Estatística, ratificada por São Tomé e Príncipe em 2016" [its commitment to consolidating a robust, modern statistical system aligned with... the African Charter on Statistics, ratified by São Tomé and Príncipe in 2016], and "o SEN deve ainda respeitar os 6 princípios da Carta Africana de Estatística (CAE)" [the National Statistical System must still respect the 6 principles of the African Charter on Statistics]. No AFRISTAT, CEEAC, or ECCAS mention found in this newer document; CPLP appears only in the acronym glossary, not substantively connected to CPI/methodology.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational strategy document (2025-2029 planning horizon).

reports.title: Lei n.º 10/2022 (revisão da Lei n.º 1/2010, Estatuto Político-Administrativo da Região Autónoma do Príncipe)
reports.publisher: Assembleia Regional do Príncipe / Assembleia Nacional
reports.description: UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF lead-chase round, following AF/G.23's open lead): Lei n.º 16/92's own full text remains unlocated, but its title, date and gazette locator are now confirmed via a government-authored INDEX entry — NOT the law's primary text — hosted on asg-plp.org (Associação dos Secretários-Gerais dos Parlamentos de Língua Portuguesa, a third-party host): São Tomé's own Assembleia Nacional documentation service (Direcção de Serviços de Apoio Parlamentar e Documentação, DSAPD/DDIP), in its September 2007 "Sumário das Legislações Publicadas nos Diários da República: 1975-2007" (section "Impostos"), lists: "Lei n.º16/92, de 31 de Dezembro de 1992, DR. n.º 27. - Lei das Finanças Locais." This confirms Lei 16/92's title is "Lei das Finanças Locais" (Local Finance Law) — a general local-government finance law, distinct from but complementary to this Príncipe-specific statute lineage — and situates it as the capstone of a coordinated December 1992 package: Lei 10/92 (autarquias framework, 9 Set 1992), Lei 11/92 (autarquia-body electoral law, 9 Set 1992), Lei 12/92 (electoral rolls, 9 Out 1992), Lei 15/92 (tax-legislation authorization, 4 Nov 1992), Lei 16/92 (this finance law, 31 Dez 1992), Lei 17/92 (1993 state budget, 31 Dez 1992). Evidentiary tier: this is a government-authored INDEX/summary entry (title + date + gazette locator only), not the statute's own primary legal text, so no separate node is minted for Lei 16/92 from this alone — see the corresponding _dropped no-document entry in st-leadchase-lei16-92.json. Original finding follows. The island of Príncipe has Autonomous Region status with its own elected Regional Government and Regional Assembly (since 1995), a genuinely federal-like fiscal relationship despite the country's small size. Hosted on principe.gov.st (the regional government's own official site). Article 101 ("Transferências orçamentais"): "Em cumprimento do princípio da solidariedade consagrado neste Estatuto e na Lei, o Orçamento Geral do Estado de cada ano inclui verbas a transferir para a Região Autónoma do Príncipe, nos termos estabelecidos na Lei n.º 16/92, de 31 de Dezembro—Lei de Finanças Locais e Regionais" [In compliance with the principle of solidarity enshrined in this Statute and the Law, the General State Budget each year includes funds to be transferred to the Príncipe Autonomous Region, under Law 16/92 of 31 December — Local and Regional Finance Law]. Articles 87 (solidarity principle, cost-sharing) and 89 (financial autonomy via State Budget transfers) corroborate.

dependencies.basis: São Tomé and Príncipe's 2018-2021 statistics strategy directly credits AFRISTAT with capacity-building work specifically on the country's harmonised CPI: "Peritos do AFRISTAT e outros consultores puderam melhorar o nível do pessoal responsável pelas contas nacionais e IHPC." 'cites' rather than 'methodology_depends_on' because the claim is about staff capacity-building, not a stated methodology dependency — matching the convention used for similar support-mention findings this session (Guinea, Madagascar). `afristat-ihpc-guide-2014` reused per the branch's node-id discipline.

INE-STP's own current national strategy states a direct compliance requirement: "o SEN deve ainda respeitar os 6 princípios da Carta Africana de Estatística (CAE)" [the National Statistical System must still respect the 6 principles of the African Charter on Statistics] — a governance-dependency claim comparable in directness to the Tanzania precedent (Statistics Act defining "international standards" by reference to the Charter). `african-charter-statistics-2009` reused (3rd country this session, after Tanzania and The Gambia).
